title: Lesson 24: Troubleshooting in Production: Diagnosing a Broken Agent Without Breaking It More
description: Diagnostic discipline for a broken agent in production: preserve the evidence before changing anything, change one variable at a time, keep a rollback you can actually use, and keep the client in the loop through the incident.

questions.question: What is the first move when diagnosing a live failure?
options: Restart the gateway to clear the failure state
Change the most likely configuration key and observe the effect
Tell the client the fix is complete to stop the questions
Preserve the evidence before changing the system
questions.explanation: The first action taken to fix a problem often destroys the evidence needed to understand it, so you secure the record before touching anything.

questions.question: What makes a change diagnostic instead of a gamble?
options: You change several variables at once so the symptom clears sooner
You change one variable, verify it, and keep a rollback ready
You change only the provider model and never the configuration
You restart the process before making any configuration change
questions.explanation: One change and one check at a time means that when the fix works you know the single cause, and a checkpoint makes each step reversible.

questions.question: When is a whole-gateway restart the right repair?
options: When a job fails on every run because its provider key is invalid
When a skill is misconfigured and fails whenever it loads
When the agent is looping or holds a poisoned connection
When a scheduled job's configuration cannot succeed at startup
questions.explanation: A restart clears live-process state, so it fits a stuck loop or poisoned connection; against a persistent misconfiguration it just repeats the same failure with less evidence.
